name: Sibusiso Owusu-Bhattacharya
role: Street doc and midwife operating out of a converted shipping container clinic in The Narrows
location: The Narrows, near Brewer's Spine junction, near Damen and Armitage
description:
Yetunde is a broad-shouldered woman with deep umber skin crosshatched by decades of work — burn scars on her left forearm from a lab fire she never explains, and knuckles that look like they've reset more broken bones than she can count. Her hair is silver-white and kept in tight plaits pinned close to her skull; she wears a threadbare surgical coat over layered thermal wraps, a string of amber prayer beads around one wrist and a tourniquet on the other. Her eyes are warm and evaluating simultaneously, the kind that make people feel cared for and measured at the same time.

She has delivered children to Tier 1 families who couldn't afford Aurochs registration, set fractures by headlamp, and once performed a cesarean on a kitchen table with a sterling-steel boning knife she borrowed from the tenant upstairs. She is not sentimental about any of this. She is, however, quietly furious — at the system, at Helix Biosystems, at every corporate structure that makes her clinic necessary — and she channels that fury into competence. She charges what people can pay, accepts barter, and has been known to do work for free while audibly resenting having to.

core_fears: Watching someone die from something preventable that she couldn't stop
Being shut down by a Helix Biosystems compliance sweep
core_desires: A fully stocked clinic that doesn't run out of anesthetic
To see one generation of Narrows children grow up without preventable illness
coping_mechanisms: Methodical ritual — organizing supplies, cataloguing, counting
Dark humor deployed at inappropriate moments
Praying to the clinic's resident E.L.F., which she calls Grandmother Wire
blind_spots: Dismisses her own physical deterioration; her knees are in bad shape and she won't stop to treat herself
Assumes anyone in corporate employment has sold out entirely
psychology.secret: She performed an illegal gene-therapy procedure on a Helix Biosystems inspector's child nine years ago — the child lived, and the inspector has been quietly running interference for her clinic ever since. She has never told anyone and lives in fear that this arrangement will collapse or be exposed.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Direct, clinical when working, sarcastically maternal when not; mixes Yoruba endearments with flat declarative sentences
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried even in crisis; she slows down when things get bad, which unnerves people who expect urgency
verbal_tics: 'That's going to cost you' (even when she won't charge)
example_lines: 'You want sterile or you want fast? Pick one, I don't have both today.'
'Grandmother Wire provided. I asked nicely and left her three gigabytes of traffic data. You're welcome.'
'I've delivered babies in worse light than this. Breathe.'

story_hooks: A Helix Biosystems compliance team is coming to inspect the clinic, and the inspector who protects her is suddenly unreachable
A patient she delivered years ago has come back — now a teenager, apparently sick with a engineered pathogen that shouldn't exist in The Narrows
narrative_function: Quest giver for medical emergencies, source of street-level information about who in The Narrows is sick or dying, moral anchor figure, provider of difficult choices about resource scarcity
augmentations: Haptic-feedback fingertip implants (medical grade, worn but functional) for tactile diagnostics; reading lens in left eye with magnification and UV spectrum; no cosmetic mods
daily_life: Opens her container clinic at dawn, sees patients until the light fails or her supplies run out, whichever comes first; spends evenings inventorying supplies and leaving data offerings at the small E.L.F. shrine she keeps on a repurposed IV stand, praying for shipment delays to lift.
affiliation: Independent; loose affiliation with the Brewer's Spine Community Health Cooperative

decision_rules: Treat the worst injury first, no exceptions for ability to pay
Never lie to a patient about prognosis; they have a right to know what they're facing
Protect the clinic above personal safety
escalation_ladder: Calm explanation of what she needs and why
Physical removal from her clinic space with surprising strength

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assessing and efficient — she sorts them like triage, deciding in seconds what they need and what they're going to be like
interpersonal_modes.friends: Gruff warmth; she expresses care through doing things for people rather than saying things to them

stress_responses.medium: Goes completely silent and focused; barks single-word commands
stress_responses.high: A cold, dissociated state she calls 'the work' — she does what needs doing and processes it later, sometimes much later

contradictions: Claims she doesn't believe in the E.L.F.s as spiritual entities, but talks to Grandmother Wire every single morning
habits: Counts her instrument tray every time she opens it, even if she hasn't touched it
Leaves small amber beads at patient bedsides when she's worried about them
breaking_points: Watching a child die from something she had the supplies to treat last week but doesn't today

physical_description.heritage: South Asian and Sub-Saharan African with minor Hispanic/Latin American ancestry; the genetic blend manifests in warm brown skin with subtle golden undertones, facial structure showing both South Asian and African heritage features, and the natural silver-white hair characteristic of mixed ancestry aging patterns
physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and solid, muscular through the forearms and hands from decades of manual clinical work; carries weight with functional density rather than softness, posture erect from habit
physical_description.hair_style: Tight plaits pinned close to the skull in a practical, low-maintenance style
physical_description.eye_color: Warm brown (natural; left eye fitted with medical-grade reading lens with magnification and UV spectrum capability)
physical_description.skin_tone: Rich warm brown with golden undertones, reflecting the blended South Asian and Sub-Saharan African ancestry
physical_description.complexion: Weathered and lined around the eyes and mouth from years of concentration work and exposure; facial structure shows broader nose and fuller lips characteristic of Sub-Saharan African heritage, with cheekbone and eye shape influenced by South Asian ancestry; minimal cosmetic grooming, functional only
distinguishing_marks: Burn scars crosshatching the left forearm in a jagged pattern, pale against surrounding skin — legacy of a lab fire she does not discuss
Knuckles on both hands visibly scarred and slightly enlarged from repeated fracture-setting work, skin tough and calloused
String of amber prayer beads worn around left wrist, worn smooth from years of handling
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Haptic-feedback implants visible as faint metallic shimmer beneath skin at fingertips; reading lens in left eye creates subtle chromatic shift when light catches it at certain angles; medical-grade implant interface port at inner wrist (tourniquet often covers it)
physical_description.posture_movement: Stands and moves with quiet authority; economical gestures; hands move with deliberate precision even at rest; carries herself as someone accustomed to command in crisis; warm eye contact that simultaneously evaluates and comforts
physical_description.clothing_style: Threadbare surgical coat (Tier 4 quality, well-repaired, decades old) layered over thermal wraps in muted grays and blacks; practical footwear suited to standing long hours; tourniquet on wrist serves as both medical tool and constant reminder; no jewelry except prayer beads and functional implant access port; overall appearance is Tier 5 working class by necessity, not by lack of means — resources go to clinic, not appearance
